'''Elazar Gutmanas''' ([[Hebrew]]: '''אלעזר גוטמנאס'''; October 28, 1939 - October 26, 2019) was an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[physicist]], [[material scientist]] and [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] at the Faculty of Materials Science and Engineering at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Eulogy to Elazar Gutmanas, OBM |url=https://materials.technion.ac.il/en/team/eulogy-to-elazar-gutmanas/ |website=Technion - Israel Institute of Technology |language=he}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Gutmanas was born on 28 October 1939 in [[Kaunas]], [[Lithuania]], to a [[Jewish]] family. His father was a journalist, translator, and English teacher, and his mother was a physics lecturer at a university and at a technological Institute in [[Vilnius]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2019-10-30 |title=In Memoriam: Professor Elazar Gutmanas |url=https://www.advancedsciencenews.com/in-memoriam-professor-elazar-gutmanas/ |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Advanced Science News |language=en-US}}</ref>

On June 24, 1941, during the [[German occupation of Lithuania during World War II|German occupation of Lithuania in World War II]], Gutmanas family boarded the last train to leave the city, and they moved to [[Kazakhstan]], [[Soviet Union]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1962, Gutmanas graduated from the Leningrad Polytechnic Institute (now [[Peter the Great St. Petersburg Polytechnic University]], SPbPU) and in 1970 he received his [[PhD]] from the Russian [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Russia)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] (ISSP).<ref name=":0" />

In 1973, Gutmanas immigrated to [[Israel]] with his family, and a year later, he joined the Department of Materials Engineering at the Technion. He remained there for the rest of his academic career.

During his years at the Technion, Gutmanas supervised graduating students, published more than one hundred articles in [[academic journal]]s, and participated in numerous international conferences. Gutmanas served as a visiting scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] (MPI-FKF).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Shpigel |first=Noa |title=מת מפצעיו החוקר שנפגע קשה בפיצוץ במעבדה בטכניון |url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/news/education/2019-10-26/ty-article/0000017f-e566-df2c-a1ff-ff7768fa0000 |website=[[Haaretz]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=פרופ׳ אמריטוס גוטמנאס אלעזר ז"ל |url=https://materials.technion.ac.il/he/team/%D7%A4%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%A4%D7%B3-%D7%90%D7%9E%D7%A8%D7%99%D7%98%D7%95%D7%A1-%D7%90%D7%9C%D7%A2%D7%96%D7%A8-%D7%92%D7%95%D7%98%D7%9E%D7%A0%D7%90%D7%A1-%D7%96%D7%9C/ |website=Technion - Israel Institute of Technology |language=he}}</ref> In 1994, he was appointed as a professor at the Technion Institute.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Ahia |first=Rabad |date=November 2019 |title=מת מפצעיו הפרופסור שנפגע בפיצוץ בטכניון |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-5613546,00.html |website=[[ynet]] |language=he}}</ref>

== Death ==
On 13 October 2019, Gutmanas worked with [[hydrogen]] at his [[laboratory]] on the Technion Institute.<ref name=":2" /> Following a [[Hydrogen leak testing|hydrogen leak]] at the place, an explosion occurred, and Elazar was critically injured. He was evacuated to [[Rambam Health Care Campus]] in [[Haifa]] where he succumbed to his injuries 13 days later on 26 October 2019.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=פויר |first=דרור |date=2019-11-01 |title=דרור פויר בעקבות תעלומת הניסוי האחרון של פרופ' גוטמנאס |url=https://www.globes.co.il/news/article.aspx?did=1001305365 |access-date=2026-03-23 |work=Globes}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Work ==
Gutmanas contributed to the field of hard protective coatings through his invention of the powder immersion reaction-assisted coating (PIRAC) method. He also attempted to find new approaches for [[self-propagating high-temperature synthesis]] (SHS).<ref name=":1" />
